topic: Namespaces and Scope Resolution in C++
explanation: Namespaces in C++ are used to organize code into logical groups and prevent name collisions, especially in large projects or when integrating multiple libraries. The scope resolution operator (::) allows explicit access to names within a specific namespace or the global namespace, clarifying which declaration is being referenced. Proper understanding of namespace scope and resolution is essential for managing symbol visibility and avoiding ambiguity in complex C++ programs.
